sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the company page
sections.what: Brings in the tools this page needs: React state helpers, the link component, the shared header and footer, the company list functions, the profile reader and the model settings reader. Marks the whole page to run in the browser.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page reads and saves data in the browser, so it needs these helpers.

sections.name: Discovered
sections.title: Shape of an AI suggested company
sections.what: Describes one AI suggestion: name, regions, sector, careers web address, reason, seniority fit, and whether it is selected.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the suggestion list a fixed shape so the rest of the page can rely on those fields.
sections.watch_out: The shape is only a promise: the server's data is not checked against it, so a missing field shows as blank.

sections.name: REGION_LABELS
sections.title: Region display names
sections.what: Maps internal region codes to readable names used in dropdowns and in the discovery request.
sections.why: Likely reason: short codes are stored, and people see full names.
sections.watch_out: A new region must also be added to the allowed list in the add suggestions function, or it will be dropped silently.

sections.name: SECTOR_LABELS
sections.title: Sector display names
sections.what: Maps internal sector codes to readable labels used in dropdowns and tags.
sections.why: Likely reason: the same as region names, codes are stored and labels are shown.
sections.watch_out: A new sector must also be added to the allowed list in the add suggestions function, or it is replaced with AI and Emerging.

sections.name: CompaniesPage, inputStyle, selectStyle, tagStyle (part 1)
sections.title: Page memory and AI company discovery
sections.what: Sets up the page's memory: the company list, filters, the add form and the discovery results. When discovery is pressed, it reads the profile and stops with a message if none exists. It then sends the profile, the chosen region and a count of 25 to the discovery route, and loads the suggestions as selected. Provider settings are only sent when the provider is not Together.
sections.why: Likely reason: the profile is sent so suggestions fit the user's background, and provider settings let the server use the model the user chose.
sections.watch_out: The provider settings include the API key in the request body, so this request must only go to the app's own server route.

sections.name: CompaniesPage, inputStyle, selectStyle, tagStyle (part 2)
sections.title: Adding suggestions and managing the list
sections.what: Turns selected suggestions into saved companies, skipping any whose name is already in the list, and adds https to a web address when it is missing. Also turns companies on or off, removes one, resets to the default list after a confirmation prompt, and saves the manual add form.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the list clean and lets the user choose which companies the job scan searches.
sections.watch_out: Company ids come from the name, so adding a company with the same name as an existing one gives it the same id, and the manual add form does not check for duplicates.

sections.name: CompaniesPage, inputStyle, selectStyle, tagStyle (part 3)
sections.title: Page header and filter controls
sections.what: Shows the title with a count of enabled companies out of the total, the discover, add, reset and back buttons, dropdowns to filter by region and sector, a checkbox to show enabled companies only, and any discovery error message.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user narrow a long list of companies.
sections.watch_out: Filters only change what is displayed; the job scan uses every enabled company, not just the filtered ones.

sections.name: CompaniesPage, inputStyle, selectStyle, tagStyle (part 4)
sections.title: AI suggestion cards and manual add form
sections.what: Shows suggested companies as selectable cards with sector, seniority fit, regions, reason and careers address. Buttons let the user select all, select none, add the selected ones, or dismiss the list. Below, a form adds one company by hand, and it can only be saved once a name and careers address are filled in.
sections.why: Likely reason: the user reviews AI suggestions before anything is saved.
sections.watch_out: Dismiss clears every suggestion at once, with no undo.

sections.name: CompaniesPage, inputStyle, selectStyle, tagStyle (part 5)
sections.title: Company cards and shared styles
sections.what: Draws the tracked companies as a grid of cards. Each card shows the company name, sector, job board system and its tenant name, and regions, plus a checkbox to turn the company on or off, a VISIT link to its careers page, and a REMOVE button. Disabled companies appear faded. The end of the section also defines the shared look for input boxes, dropdowns and small tag labels used earlier in the page.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user scan the list and act on each company without leaving the page. Reason for the shared style objects not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Each card's checkbox and REMOVE button depend on the toggle and remove handlers defined earlier in the file, so those names must stay in sync.

summary: The company list page where the user keeps the companies the job scan searches, and can ask AI to suggest more.
purpose: Lets the user view, filter, turn on or off, add, remove and reset target companies, and add companies suggested by AI.
why: Likely reason: the job scan only looks at enabled companies, so the user needs direct control over that list.
how: 1. Loads the saved company list when the page opens. 2. Lets the user filter by region, sector or enabled status. 3. On discover, sends the saved profile and model settings to the discovery route and shows the suggestions as selected. 4. Adding selected suggestions or a manual entry saves the new companies into the list. 5. Turning on or off, removing and resetting each rewrite the whole list the same way.
inputs: The saved company list, the saved profile, the saved model settings (provider, model and key), the chosen region, and the user's clicks and typed fields.
outputs: An updated saved company list, a request to the discovery route, and on-screen suggestions and error messages.
risks: The provider API key is sent in the request body from the browser. Company ids are made from names, so adding a company with the same name as an existing one can clash. Reset removes custom additions after a confirmation. The last section of the file (outline item s9) was not provided, so it was not reviewed.
debug: If discovery fails, read the error text above the list, then check the discovery route. If the scan ignores a company, check its enabled switch and region. If a suggestion does not appear in the list, check whether a company with the same name already exists. If the list looks wrong after reset, check the reset function in the company targets library.
